Subject: Zonal burst capacity & credits — proposal request

Hi Lauren,

Quick context: we run a financial data product that hits high burstiness around US market open/close and during earnings windows. We're evaluating Dedicated capacity with a burst/autoscale overlay and need a commercial proposal that reflects:

- Regionally segmented burst pools (we want separate caps for us-west and us-east for latency reasons)
- Clear cooldown definitions and a suggested grace period for short spikes (we measured 30–90s bursts in our traces)
- Pricing for burst beyond reserved throughput and an approach for credits/refunds if purchased burst goes unused in a month
- Any minimums or pro-rata rules if we change committed throughput mid-quarter

Our target committed throughput: ~1.2M tokens/day (steady) but peaks can be 6–8x for up to 10 minutes. We care about predictable unit economics and keeping tail latency under 250ms for 95th percentile.

Can you send a short proposal (numbers and high-level mechanics) and a clean slide or sheet we can share with procurement? We're on a tight Q2 review cycle.

Thanks,

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear brief, very helpful.

Summary of what we can do and next steps:

1) Zonal burst pools: we can offer per-region burst overlays (US-WEST / US-EAST) with independent caps and monitoring. This prevents cross-region exhaustion and keeps regional latency guarantees.

2) Grace & cooldown: default cooldown window is 10 minutes. We can add a 90-second "grace corridor" for sub-minute spikes where no billing is applied and requests are served from short-term prefix/KV cache (good for the 30–90s spikes you described).

3) Pricing & credits: three commercial levers — reserved commit (per-month), usable burst credits (pre-purchased credits applied at surge rates), and on-demand burst (pay-as-you-go surge rate).
   - Proposal sheet attached with example numbers and a model for pro-rata crediting for unused purchased burst.
   - If you pre-buy burst credits and consume <50% in the billing month, we propose automatic 50% carryover as a credit to the next 30 days (can extend to 90 days via contract).

4) Mid-quarter changes: we can pro-rate committed throughput adjustments; any downward change has a 30-day notice to avoid churn complexity.

Next: Ben will follow up with sizing guidance and a technical note. I'll prepare a single-sheet commercial summary for procurement. Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow to go line-by-line?

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Zonal burst capacity & credits — proposal request (technical note)

Lauren / Natalie / Karthik — technical follow-up with sizing and operational mechanics so pricing maps to capacity correctly. High level points below; see attached sizing CSV for the model inputs.

- GPU pool sizing: for your steady 1.2M tokens/day and 6–8x short peaks, recommend a baseline Dedicated pool sized for 2.5x steady throughput to give headroom for sustained bursts. Overlay zonal burst pools provision elastic instances that spin up in <60s for larger events.

- Headroom multiplier: use a 2.5x baseline with a zonal overlay that can add an additional 3–4x for short surges. Overlay capacity is metered separately and billed at surge rate tiers.

- Cooldown & grace mechanics:
  * Grace corridor: first 90s after a cold spike — served from hot cache; no burst billing.
  * Primary cooldown: 10 minute cooldown after overlay scaling event — during cooldown subsequent bursts incur reduced-rate billing at 50% of normal surge rate until the cooldown ends. This reduces double-billing for back-to-back spikes.

- Billing model specifics:
  * Pre-purchased burst credits are consumed first. If credits depleted, fall back to on-demand surge rate.
  * Pro-rata crediting: unused pre-purchased burst credits can be carried forward at 50% value for 30 days, or 70% value for 90 days with an annual commitment.
  * Blended cap: we can cap blended monthly surge charges at a configurable % of committed spend (recommend 40% cap to bound cost spikes).

- SLAs & latency: to keep p95 <250ms we recommend placing routing policy to prefer regional pool and failover to nearest region only on capacity exhaustion.

I'll be on the call and can walk through the CSV metrics and cost curves. (attachment: capacity-sizing.csv)

—Ben
